About us

Manatū Taonga Ministry for Culture and Heritage’s purpose is Ki te puāwai te ahurea, Ka ora te iwi | Culture is thriving, The people are well. Manatū Taonga leads government work in the arts, heritage, sports and broadcasting sectors. The Ministry supports many of Aotearoa New Zealand’s cultural sector organisations; advises government on cultural matters and provides research and resources for everyone to access. The organisations it funds deliver a wide range of cultural experiences for all to enjoy.

    We are delighted to announce three new members have been appointed to the Te Papa Board. Professor Richard Douglas MNZM is an internationally recognised ear nose and throat surgeon and founder of the Tarāpunga Charitable Trust, which provides healthcare access for remote communities in Te Tai Tokerau. Richard is a long-standing philanthropic supporter of the arts, and has his own creative practice as a landscape photographer. Professor James Belich ONZM is a renowned New Zealand historian and academic best known for his groundbreaking work on the New Zealand Wars and settler colonialism, which has had a profound effect on how the public understands indigenous military innovation and British colonial expansion. James serves as an Emeritus Professor of History at the University of Oxford and a Professorial Fellow at Balliol College. Dr. Wendy Nelson MNZM is an internationally acclaimed phycologist or seaweed scientist. She is currently an Honorary Academic and Professor of Biological Sciences at the University of Auckland and previously served for over two decades as a Principal Scientist at NIWA, the National Institute of Water and Atmospheric Research. Wendy knows Te Papa well, having spent 15 years at the museum as a curator of Botany. We look forward to the wisdom, experience, and passion each of them brings to the governance of Te Papa Tongarewa alongside Manatū Taonga Ministry for Culture and Heritage

    We’re proud to share new insights into volunteering for arts, culture, and heritage activities across Aotearoa 💙 Our latest report explores who volunteers, what they do, and what motivates them - highlighting the vital role volunteers play in bringing events, creativity and community experiences to life. Key findings include: 🔍 Nearly 1 in 4 New Zealanders volunteer in arts, culture, and heritage - a powerful reminder of the people who make it all happen behind the scenes. 🔍 Young adults (18 – 29 years) are leading the way, with the highest participation rates of any age group (35%) 🔍 Cultural festivals and event support is the most common volunteering activity across all groups These insights help build a clearer picture of how people are engaging - and how we can better support and grow volunteering across our sectors. 🔗 Read the full report: https://lnkd.in/edj6Vi2G As we kick off National Volunteer Week 2026, we acknowledge the incredible contribution of volunteers across the motu - thank you for the time, energy and passion you bring to our communities 🙌 #NVW2026 #volunteersareamazing #VolunteeringNZ Volunteering New Zealand | Tūao Aotearoa

    Steven Fyfe and Melissa King have been appointed to the New Zealand Symphony Orchestra Board and began their three-year terms on 1 May.   Steven Fyfe has had an extensive executive career within the banking, finance, and investment sector, including eight years as Chief Financial Officer at the National Bank, and latterly has held a range of governance roles including eight years as a Trustee of Royal New Zealand Ballet. He is currently an independent member of the NZSO Audit Committee. Mr Fyfe replaces Edwin Read, whose term on the Board ended on 30 April.   Melissa King is an experienced Orchestra Executive who is currently Director of Artistic Planning at the Sydney Symphony Orchestra. She has also held similar senior roles with the Melbourne Symphony Orchestra, and the NZSO. Melissa’s international perspective and ability to build relationships across the sector will be a great addition to the Board. Furthermore, NZSO Board Chair Carmel Walsh has been reappointed from 1 May to 30 June 2028, and Susannah Robinson appointed Deputy Chair from 1 May to 30 September 2027.

    Whakamihi (Congratulations) to Rowena Davenport and Gina Mills on their appointments as new members of the Sport New Zealand Ihi Aotearoa Board.     Rowena Davenport is an experienced independent director with governance roles across finance, legal, government, education, and sport. She is Deputy Chair of Otago Polytechnic Council, a Founding Director of the Matatū Advisory Board, and a board member for Finance Now, AWS Legal, the Highlanders, and the Halberg Foundation. Rowena has also been appointed Deputy Chair of the Sport New Zealand Board. Gina Mills is an executive leader and Head of Leadership and Culture at Southern Cross Health Insurance. She serves on the SPCA board and has held governance roles across sport and professional bodies. A Chartered Member of the Institute of Directors and ICAEW Fellow, she previously spent over 20 years in senior roles at EY.

    📣 We’re seeking a new Chair for the Sport Integrity Commission Te Kahu Raunui Board. On behalf of the Minister for Sport and Recreation, we’re excited to invite expressions of interest for the role of Chair of the Sport Integrity Commission Te Kahu Raunui Board. This is a chance to help shape the future of sport and recreation in Aotearoa - guiding strategy, driving performance, and representing an organisation built on trust, fairness, and integrity. The Sport Integrity Commission is an independent Crown entity dedicated to making sport and recreation in New Zealand safer, fairer, and worthy of the confidence of every participant and supporter.     Whakamihi (Congratulations) to Dale Aotea Stephens and Rāniera (Daniel) Procter on their appointments to the Sport New Zealand Ihi Aotearoa Board. They will begin their terms on 1 April 2026, serving through to March 2029. Dale Stephens (Te Rarawa) is a professional director with senior leadership experience in the sports sector as former Chief  Executive for Basketball New Zealand and Touch New Zealand. He currently chairs New Zealand Māori Tourism, the Ministry of Awesome, and Destination Original Indigenous Tourism. Rāniera (Daniel) Procter (Ngāti Porou, Ngāi Tāmanuhiri, Rangitāne, Ngāti Uepōhatu) is a Gisborne-based social worker, seven‑time National Surfing Champion and fluent te reo Māori speaker. He chairs Sport NZ’s Te Taumata Māori and holds governance roles with Te Kōhanga Reo National Trust, Te Matakahuki, and Te Kura Kaupapa Māori o Ngā Uri a Māui.

    Do you know how many New Zealand creatives using digital tools use AI in their work? If you guessed 65%, you're right on the money. A new report, the Cultural Participation Survey, shows that among creators who said they use digital tools, 65% use generative AI as part of their creative process. Nearly half use these tools to support or refine their ideas, one in three to produce art and creative work, and 14% to share their creations with a wider audience/make it accessible. To read more about the survey and its findings, visit our website: https://lnkd.in/eayH4gwj

    Sunday marks seven years since of one of Aotearoa New Zealand’s darkest days – the Christchurch terror attacks – when 51 people were killed at Al Noor Mosque and Linwood Islamic Centre.  Since 2022, Manatū Taonga has worked with media to broadcast a recording of the adhan (call to prayer) at 1.39 pm each March 15, as an act of remembrance and symbol of solidarity with New Zealand’s Muslim communities. Broadcasting the adhan was specifically requested by the community directly impacted by the attacks of 15 March 2019 as an appropriate way to observe the remembrance of this tragic event.   🔗 To download a copy of the adhan recording, follow this link: https://lnkd.in/e-J4Etpf.
